goal:
Do the job below from the input files, then write one JSON file per numbered line.

The input files (label: file):
  - flights: input/flights.txt

For each numbered job line N, write ONE file output/steps/N.json: a JSON object with exactly these keys.
  "text"  — your answer for that line, as a string.
  "cites" — an object: for each input you drew on, its label as the key and a list of {"claim", "quote"} as the value.
            "claim" is one thing your text relies on; "quote" is words copied EXACTLY from that input (spacing and
            ** or __ marks do not matter). Every number in a claim must also appear in its quote.
  In each claim, copy every number, time and price exactly as the input writes it (for example "9:27 AM", not "09:27"),
  because the check matches the numbers in your claim against your quote.
A job line the brief below marks as a FACTS line is different: its file holds ONLY {"results": [{"quote": "...", "values":
{"<fact>": "<value>"}}]} — one result per thing found, one quote copied exactly from the text of that one result, the values written as the quote
writes them; no "text" and no "cites". A line the brief marks as a TEXT line keeps "text" (free words), and every number in it
must be copied from a quote of an earlier facts line.
Write nothing outside output/, and never edit the files under input/. The file must be complete, valid JSON: a file cut
off before its closing brace counts as not written.

The job, line by line:
1. List 3 flights from Boston to Chicago
   rule: under $450; not a red-eye; nonstop; departure time between 05:00 and 21:59

Job line 1 is a FACTS line. Write output/steps/1.json as {"results": [{"quote": "...", "values": {...}}]} and nothing else — no "text", no "cites".
  One result per thing you find in the input "flights": exactly 3 results.
  "quote": ONE quote per result, copied exactly from that result's own text in the input (at most 4000 characters) — never joined from two results.
  "values": one entry per fact below, written exactly as the quote writes it (for example "9:27 AM", not "09:27"; "389", not "389.00").
    - origin airport — no value to write; the quote you copy must say "Chicago O'Hare International Airport"
    - destination airport — no value to write; the quote you copy must say "Boston Logan International Airport"
    - price — an amount in US dollars, right after "From", must be under 450 US dollars
    - stops — no value to write; the quote you copy must say "Nonstop"
    - departure time — a time, right after "Departure time:", must be between 05:00 and 21:59

The plan the person confirmed: Output/output/steps/1.json lists 3 flights, each with a price under $450, \"Nonstop\", a \"Departure time:\" between 05:00 and 21:59, origin \"Chicago ORD\" and destination \"Boston BOS\", each quoted from the flights input.

steps.action: Read input/flights.txt with grep/read to locate each flight's single accessibility line of the form `- link "From <N> US dollars. Nonstop flight with <airline>. Leaves Chicago O'Hare International Airport at <time> on Friday, November 20 and arrives at Boston Logan International Airport at <other time> ... Select flight"`. Then write output/steps/1.json (create the output/steps location as part of the write) containing exactly one closed, valid JSON object {"results": [ ... ]} with exactly 3 entries and no other keys at top level — no "text", no "cites". Each entry has: "quote" — copied character for character from that one flight's own `link` line (do not concatenate it with the separate `- generic "Departure time: ..."` line, and never merge text from two different flights); the quote must literally contain `From <N> US dollars`, `Nonstop`, `Chicago O'Hare International Airport` and `Boston Logan International Airport`. Each entry's "values" is {"price": "<N written exactly as the link line writes it, e.g. 137 — no dollar sign, no .00>", "departure time": "<the departure time written exactly as printed in that same link line, e.g. 7:05 AM>"} — only these two fact keys. Choose 3 distinct flights whose price is under 450 US dollars, whose link line says Nonstop, and whose departure time is between 05:00 and 21:59 (no red-eye). Keep the file complete and valid JSON — a file cut off before its closing braces counts as not written. If the check output names this file or any other path under output/, you are free to read and rewrite it, and you may edit any file under output/ that the check reports; iterate on output/steps/1.json until the check named line-1-three-flights passes.
